candidates.exact_span: The permittee may apply for a testing frequency reduction upon the successful completion of the first four consecutive quarters of testing for a test species, with no lethal or sub-lethal effects demonstrated at or below the critical dilution. If granted, the monitoring frequency for that test species may be reduced to not less than once per year for the less sensitive species (usually the vertebrate species) and not less than twice per year for the more sensitive test species (usually the invertebrate species).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a frequency reduction was eligible and granted changes the applicable WET monitoring schedule (quarterly vs annual/semiannual), which alters which monitoring periods were required and how missing or absent WET results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must certify in writing that no test failures have occurred and that all tests meet all test acceptability criteria above. In addition, the permittee must provide a list with each test performed including test initiation date, species, and NOECs. Upon review and acceptance of this information, the agency will issue a letter of confirmation of the monitoring frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reduced monitoring frequency is operative only after written certification and agency acceptance; interpretation of whether those conditions were met changes applicable monitoring obligations, whether expected WET results exist for comparison, and whether NOEC values from the submitted list serve as the numeric basis for compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: If any test demonstrates lethal or sub-lethal effects at or below the critical dilution at any time during the life of this permit, three monthly retests are required. If a frequency reduction had been granted, the monitoring frequency for the affected test species reverts to once per quarter until the permit is re-issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether effects occurred at or below the critical dilution triggers mandatory monthly retests and reversion to quarterly monitoring, changing required monitoring periods, expected result counts, and the compliance events against which reported WET measurements must be evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: This monitoring frequency reduction applies only until the expiration date of this permit, at which time the monitoring frequency for both test species reverts to once per quarter until the permit is re-issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The timing of permit expiration within Federal FY2025 determines when reduced WET frequency ends and quarterly monitoring resumes, changing which monitoring intervals were required and how gaps in reported data should be interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: The requirements of this subsection apply only when a toxicity test demonstrates significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Persistent-toxicity obligations are conditional on a prior demonstration of significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution; different readings of that trigger change whether subsection 5 requirements were applicable and whether absent related monitoring is excused or indicates missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Significant toxic effects, are herein defined as a statistically significant difference at the 95% confidence level between the survival of the appropriate test organism in a specified effluent dilution and the control (0% effluent).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This operative definition governs when a WET result counts as a failure or significant effect, which determines whether numeric/compliance comparison applies, whether follow-on monitoring and retest duties attach, and how no-result or ambiguous WET data should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: If the initial WET test conducted fails, the permittee will conduct three retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an initial WET test is interpreted as a failure determines an additional obligation for three retests, changing the set of required monitoring events and whether missing retest data reflects a documented no-data state or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: A test that meets all test acceptability criteria and demonstrates significant toxic effects does not need additional confirmation. Such testing cannot confirm or disprove a previous test result.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when acceptability criteria are met and when confirmation is unnecessary affects whether further monitoring was required after certain WET outcomes and whether conflicting or missing follow-up results remain unresolved versus conditionally excused.
